about: The ontology of an incident on this site: eight kinds of thing and nine relations, small enough to explain on one page (README.md beside this file). tools/graph-build.mjs reads it, builds data/graph/storm.json and data/graph/tables/*.json from the incident's JSON files, and refuses a node or edge this file does not allow. Kept by incident.graph@web-summit.dinis.

every_item.about: Every node and every edge carries these four, with no exception.

fields.label: fact | evidence | hypothesis
fields.source: an https URL: where it was read (a primary channel, a press page, or the file on this site it was derived from)
fields.read: the UTC time it was read (where the file gives no time per item, the file's own time)
fields.origin: the file and the place inside it this item was built from (file#pointer)

labels.fact: read on the channel of the body that decides or warns, by us or by a named desk
labels.evidence: reported by others (press, a relayed statement, a public post), with its source; holds until a primary source says otherwise
labels.hypothesis: our analysis, with its reasons; never stated as fact

Actor.what: Someone who decides, warns or reports.

kinds.body: a public body: an authority, the government, a municipality
kinds.operator: runs a service: transport, a venue, a bridge, schools
kinds.organiser: runs the event: Web Summit and its own programmes
kinds.outlet: where others report: the press and public social platforms

Actor.id: actor:<id> (from the decision graph) or actor:host:<host> (derived from a cited or covering site)
Actor.from: decisions/graph.json nodes; outlets from the hosts of the URLs that evidence and signals cite, and from the sites covering the storm (research/weather-sites/sites.json)

Decision.what: Something an actor decided, or has not yet announced (status says which).

Warning.what: A warning from a body that warns: issued (the moment it was made or first read) or in force (its type, level, area, start and end).
Warning.from: decisions/graph.json edges by IPMA and ANEPC's avisos; weather/warnings.json (in force); weather/cap.json (phase cap: IPMA's own messages, with the time IPMA sent each)

Signal.what: A row of the incident's timeline: something published, said or observed, at a time.

Source.what: A URL that was read: a page, a feed, an API.
Source.from: decisions/sources.json; every other URL an item cites; the pages covering the storm (research/weather-sites/sites.json, coverage says what kind)

Place.what: Where a warning applies: an IPMA warning area (a district) or mainland Portugal.
Place.from: weather/warnings.json areas; names from IPMA's list of districts (data/graph/ref/ipma-areas.json)

Dataset.what: A JSON file of the incident, served on this site and under api/v1/.

Agent.what: An agent or desk that reads sources and writes datasets.
Agent.from: data/keys.json; the read_by and updated_by fields of the datasets

decides.what: the actor made (or owes) this decision

reports.what: the actor published it: an outlet reporting a decision, a body publishing on its own channel

cites.what: the item was read at this URL (or is corroborated by it)

precedes.what: time order between two items the researcher linked (follows); carries lead_minutes when both times are known to the minute. Order only: it does not claim cause

attributes.lead_minutes: minutes from the earlier to the later; null when either time is unknown or known only to the day

affects.what: the actors a decision touches (the researcher's `to`)

located-in.what: a warning's area; a district inside mainland Portugal

produced-by.what: who made it: a dataset by the agent that keeps it, a source by the actor whose channel it is

issued-as.what: the same warning, opened: a warning as the researcher recorded it (or as it stands in force) and the body's own message that carries it (IPMA's CAP message, with the time IPMA sent it). The step from a warning to its issue

own_channels.about: The one hand-kept list the builder uses. A host is an actor's own channel when the researcher read the actor there as a fact; these hosts are added because they are plainly the actor's own although its node was read through the press. not_outlets: hosts that carry files, not reporting; they never become an outlet.

public_posts.about: The default is to withhold: a personal post address on a social platform never enters the graph or a table (the builder keeps the host only). Each exception is named here by the timeline row it belongs to, with the reason and who decided. The researcher's listed official channels (decisions/sources.json) need no entry.

rows.reason: public figure in a public role

not_in_the_graph: People. No private person is a node; journalists and officials are not modelled here (incident.media@ keeps by-lines on public articles in its own files). Forecast values and observations stay in weather/*.json: the graph links the dataset, not each number.
not_a_warning_service: The graph records what authorities decided and warned, and when we read it. It is not a forecast and gives no advice: follow IPMA and ANEPC.
grammar: Every edge is a verb with a distinct inverse (relations.<verb>.inverse); there is no generic 'related to' edge. The whole graph is never drawn: a view is the result of a question. A node opens into its own graph (a warning into IPMA's messages for it, a decision into what it followed and where it was read). After graphs.sgit.ai (meaning through connectivity) and Fractal Semantic Graphs.

crossings.about: How this graph joins the site's other graphs without copying them. Each world keeps its own kinds, verbs and ids; nothing of theirs becomes a node here. A crossing is a named edge with an inverse from a node of this graph to a thing in another world, written as <world>/<its own id> and opened on that world's own page. One thing has one id in each world and the entity id is the pivot: where the other world declares the same entity as this graph's node, the crossing is a fact; where the builder matched by host, it is a hypothesis and says why. Built into data/graph/crossings.json by tools/graph-build.mjs; never written by hand.

entities.what: Everything a page can mention, with a page each (incident.entities@).
entities.joined_by: its `graph` field names this graph's node; the node carries `entity`

sources.what: The register of outside bodies this site takes data from or cites, with each licence as published (incident.sources@).
sources.joined_by: its `entity` field, through entities/index.json; otherwise one of its hosts

meteorology.what: The weather data supply chain: bodies, observing systems, models, datasets, warning services and sites, with its own ten verbs (incident.meteorology@).
meteorology.joined_by: the host of a body's address

evidence.what: Wayback: our own dated captures of outside pages and feeds (incident.archivist@).

registered-as.what: the actor's entry in the register of sources: what it publishes, what we take, its licence as published

in-lineage-as.what: the same body in the weather data supply chain, where its models, observing systems and services are

issued-through.what: the warning service this warning came through; from there the supply chain runs down to the models and the instruments. Derived: the body that warns issues one warning service of its own

kept-as.what: our latest dated capture of the address an item was read at: the last step before the outside address. Held once per address in crossings.json `captures`, not once per item
